ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution characterized by a predominantly low-intensity (dark) fluke surface (>85%) and high-intensity (white) localized pixel clusters representing scars and biofouling.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous low-intensity dark region across both lobes. Discontinuous high-intensity focal points (circular) and linear streaks are mapped across the surface. Specific high-intensity geometric clusters are located at the distal tips of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Central V-shaped depression with a defined vertex; the angle is approximately 110 degrees with a clear vertical depth separating the two fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude micro-serrations along the continuous linear boundary. Distal segments exhibit larger irregular indentations, particularly on the outer lateral margin of the left lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curves fitted to the upper trailing edges, transitioning into tapered, irregular distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Spatial detection of approximately 12 high-contrast circular pixel clusters distributed across the dark field, including a prominent pair of circles on the upper-right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Numerous unaligned, high-intensity linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) ranging from 10 to 50 pixels in length, oriented horizontally and diagonally across the fluke surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Heavy high-intensity encrustations (barnacle colonies) present at the extreme distal tips of both lobes. Significant jagged tissue loss/indentation on the lateral edge of the left lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique textural density at the fluke tips characterized by multi-layered, high-frequency pixel variations distinct from the smoother intensity mapping of the central fluke body.
